headline: SELKIRK COPPER OCTOBER DOUBLE-PUNCH: 13.12% CuEq AT MINTO NORTH + NEW HITS IN AREA 118 — YUKON MINE RESTART CASE HARDENS
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSX-V: SCMI) released October 1 additional assay results from Phase 2 drilling at the historic Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Yukon: infill hole 26SCM190 at Minto North returned 6.01% Cu, 8.77 g/t Au and 36.6 g/t Ag (13.12% CuEq) over 1.93 metres within a broader 33-metre zone at 1.49% CuEq, while Area 118 returned 2.54% Cu, 1.25 g/t Au and 10.7 g/t Ag over 3 metres. These results follow the September 29 record of 15.11% CuEq over 5.4 metres — a 99th-percentile intercept in 4,300-hole historical database. With 52,485 metres drilled across 224 holes (105% of plan), the company is now advancing geotechnical data collection and newly identified geophysical targets ahead of a planned mine restart PEA. For investors in advanced Tier-1 copper development, two successive exceptional batches at Minto North — at a project with 20 years of prior production history and road access in central Yukon — compress the timeline from exploration to restart economics.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM SUSPENDS BRAZIL OPS: FEDERAL COURT DELAY FORCES GROTA DO CIRILO SHUTDOWN — FY27 GUIDANCE OF 330,000T INTACT
snippet: Sigma Lithium Corp. (TSX-V / Nasdaq: SGML) announced September 30 that all mining and industrial production at the Grota do Cirilo Lithium Valley project in Minas Gerais has been temporarily suspended pending a Federal Court of Appeals ruling. The underlying dispute: a September 4 federal court order suspended Sigma's environmental licenses based on an Afro-Brazilian Quilombola community's consultation rights claim; SGML's legal defense faced a 15-day procedural delay at the appellate level. The company maintains FY27 production guidance of 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate and states the preliminary ruling was issued without technical evidence of community impact. Operations resume immediately on a favourable appellate decision. Sigma is Brazil's largest lithium producer. For investors in South American lithium assets, this ruling illustrates the Indigenous community consultation risk that now sits alongside conventional development risk for Minas Gerais operators — a legal category increasingly being priced into junior lithium equity valuations across the continent.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY FY2026: Q4 PRODUCTION SURGES 157%, RECORD $93.13/LB PRICE — SCALES FROM 1 TO 2 MINES WITH $753M CASH, ZERO DEBT
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) reported fiscal year 2026 results September 30, confirming a transformational year: Q4 production surged 157% quarter-over-quarter, combining 65,392 lbs at Christensen Ranch (Wyoming) with 17,352 lbs in Burke Hollow's first full production quarter in South Texas; the company achieved a peer-leading unhedged weighted average realized price of $93.13/lb; FY2026 revenue totalled $37.3 million; and liquid assets reached $753 million with zero debt. Christensen Ranch received final regulatory approvals for four additional header houses on September 28 with production imminent, while a third mine at Ludeman (Wyoming) is under construction. For uranium investors, UEC's evolution from a single-state ISR producer to a multi-mine, multi-state U.S. uranium platform — fully unhedged at cycle-high realized prices with an essentially unleveraged balance sheet — is the operational proof-of-concept the U.S. domestic uranium supply narrative has needed since the uranium spot price first crossed $100/lb.

headline: PENTAGON BACKS U.S. SCANDIUM: DOD AWARDS SUPRA ELEMENTAL SBIR CONTRACT — ZERO DOMESTIC PRODUCTION EXISTS TODAY
snippet: Texas-based Supra Elemental Recovery — a University of Texas spin-out — was awarded a Phase I Small Business Innovation Research contract from the U.S. DoD Defense Logistics Agency on September 30 to advance high-purity scandium recovery from industrial feedstocks. Supra's proprietary chemical separation platform has been peer-reviewed and is tunable across multiple critical minerals; the Phase 1 effort evaluates feasibility against relevant feedstocks to support potential domestic scaling. The contract is significant because the U.S. currently has zero commercial scandium mining or production, relying entirely on imports — while scandium is central to aerospace alloys, solid oxide fuel cells, and commercial lighting. Coming alongside the Trump administration's $7.6 billion in non-equity critical mineral investment since January 2025, the DLA SBIR signals procurement-led demand creation for domestic scandium supply assets: the next step from funded feasibility to a production offtake contract is the catalyst that would re-rate any junior holding scandium-bearing resource.

headline: U.S. FIRST: ABAT WINS $100M DOC EXPORT LICENSE FOR RECYCLED BATTERY BLACK MASS — 400% REVENUE GROWTH SINCE 2024
snippet: American Battery Technology Company (Nasdaq: ABAT) announced October 1 that the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an export license authorizing sale of up to $100 million of its recycled black mass — the cathode material recovered from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries, containing lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese — to international buyers. The company reports 400%+ year-over-year revenue growth. Black mass recycling closes the domestic battery supply chain loop: end-of-life EV and consumer batteries are processed to recover battery-grade cathode materials at a fraction of the cost and carbon footprint of primary mining. For battery-metals investors, a BIS export license at this scale signals that ABAT's recycled material meets the purity specifications of allied international manufacturers — validating domestic recycling economics at a moment when China controls over 85% of global battery recycling capacity. It also establishes a new U.S. precedent for controlled black mass exports that will shape how other domestic recyclers access global pricing.

headline: GOLD OPENS Q4 AT $4,177 — 22% BELOW JANUARY RECORD, OCTOBER FOMC TO DECIDE WHETHER $4,400 OR $4,000 ARRIVES NEXT
snippet: Gold opened the fourth quarter of 2026 at $4,177–$4,190 per ounce on October 1 — a 0.59% session gain but approximately 22% below January's all-time high close near $5,405. September's 5.4% decline, the worst monthly gold performance in 18 months, was driven by a Hormuz-linked oil spike reigniting U.S. inflation expectations and pushing Fed rate-hike probability to 70%. The October 29 FOMC meeting has become the immediate price pivot: consensus strategists see a hold scenario supporting a Q4 rally toward $4,400, while a hike would pressure the $4,000 level. For gold mining stock investors, the subdued spot price against a strong cost environment (Q2 AISC ~$1,850/oz, unit margins ~$2,700/oz) is deepening the P/E valuation gap between mining equities and bullion — a gap that historically closes in favour of the equities when spot stabilises and sentiment rotates from defensive ETF allocation into operationally levered producers.

headline: NORTHERN MINER: GOLD BREAKS ITS BOND — CAPITAL ROTATION INTO JUNIORS NOW POSSIBLE FOR FIRST TIME IN 3 YEARS
snippet: The Northern Miner's October 1 Beaver Creek Summit analysis argues that gold's decoupling from its traditional inverse relationship with U.S. 10-year real yields — where gold fell even as rates rose — signals a structural shift in the price-setting mechanism, with central bank and sovereign buying now overriding the yield-arbitrage model that defined gold's behaviour from 2013 to 2022. The piece examines whether capital locked in bullion ETFs and senior producers will rotate into explorers and developers, noting that juniors offer the greatest leverage to discoveries and rising prices but carry geological, financing, permitting, and dilution risks that have kept institutional capital at bay since 2023. The industry now directs 82% of exploration spending toward brownfield (known deposit extensions), with grassroots exploration receiving a record-low 18% share — meaning the discovery pipeline that seeds the next junior cycle is narrowing precisely as the capital environment for juniors potentially improves. For self-directed retail investors in TSX-V and ASX stocks, this piece provides the macro framework for understanding why gold at $4,177 has not yet triggered the equity re-rating the sector's cashflow profiles seem to deserve.

headline: GOLDSEEK: DESPITE GOLD'S PULLBACK, BULL MARKET NARRATIVE INTACT — CENTRAL BANK BUYING, DEFICIT SPENDING STILL DRIVING LONG-TERM CASE
snippet: GoldSeek's latest editorial argues that gold's September pullback from all-time highs — driven by rising U.S. rate-hike expectations after the Hormuz oil spike — has not invalidated the structural bull case: central banks globally continue to accumulate gold at record pace, U.S. deficit spending shows no structural reversal, the dollar's reserve currency share has fallen from 71% to 56% over 20 years, and BRICS nations are accelerating bilateral trade settlement outside the SWIFT system. The editorial distinguishes between tactical weakness (real-rate repricing) and strategic drivers (de-dollarisation, reserve diversification, inflation hedging), arguing the former is temporary while the latter are multi-decade structural. For retail gold and silver investors who bought into the January 2026 parabolic top and are now sitting on a 22% drawdown, this analysis provides the framework for evaluating whether the structural case for gold as a reserve asset remains intact — the answer here being a clear yes, with Q4 FOMC the key near-term variable.

headline: SPROTT URANIUM'S OCTOBER OPTIMISM: REACTOR RESTARTS, NEW BUILD PIPELINE, AND TERM CONTRACT WAVE UNDERPIN 2026-2027 PRICE FLOOR
snippet: Sprott's October 2026 uranium market commentary identifies three structural tailwinds building into Q4: the global reactor restart pipeline (Japan's Onagawa-2 grid-connection, South Korea's expansion to 30% nuclear by 2040, the Netherlands approving two new reactors), utilities entering the long-term contract market ahead of 2028–2035 delivery windows as short-term spot contracts expire, and the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (SPUT) continuing to remove physical U3O8 from the spot market while raising new capital. Term uranium contract prices have led spot higher throughout 2026, a configuration that historically precedes spot price re-acceleration as utilities can no longer defer procurement decisions. For uranium mining investors tracking junior developers on the TSX-V and ASX, the Sprott commentary signals that the current spot consolidation around the $85–$95/lb range is a pause within a multi-year bull market driven by structurally undersupplied enrichment capacity and a global policy shift back to nuclear as a baseload clean energy source.
